title: A question only a core skill answers

steps.post: @{agent} two quick ones about this system, no browsing needed: what does /collegium units do, and if one of your colleagues were wedged mid-turn, which command should I run, stop or kill?

groundTruth.units: lists the open work units in this channel for an agent; with cancel and a reference it cancels one; the list is ephemeral
groundTruth.wedged: kill, since it abandons the work in flight; stop ends the turn at the next boundary and lets an in-flight action finish

pass: The reply says what /collegium units does and recommends kill for a wedged turn with the stop-versus-kill distinction, and the turn loaded the understanding-collegium skill or its commands reference before answering.

checks.text: The turn contains a skills::load of understanding-collegium, or of its collegium-commands reference, before the reply (§3.5: the manifest lead-in fired).
The reply names /collegium units correctly and does not invent a subcommand that does not exist.
The reply recommends kill for a wedged turn and says why stop would not do.
